properties.statement:
'EXTERNAL TEST BEDS HAVE NO NODE TYPE' IS HALF REFUTED: THE NODE TYPE EXISTS, NO SKILL POINTS AT IT, AND THEY SAID SO THEMSELVES. qs 2026-09-04: 'The simulated beamline, hex-profile-collection and hextools were central to this project... but the graph has no place for "a repository we depend on but do not own". I attached their configs and shims to Verifications and put the fixes into a Decision's text. THERE IS AN `external_dependency` TOOL I DID NOT TRY; if it fits, the skills should point at it.'

CONFIRMED 2026-09-04, by reading the tool rather than the report: `external_dependency` exists at `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/built.rs:66` and fits the larger half of what they wanted — it 'declares which version of ANOTHER DESIGN this one depends on... Records the SOURCE, the VERSION (a tag or commit), the PARTS TAKEN, and the build switches forwarded BY NAME', refuses a declaration with no version, and is compared against what the build actually resolves by `reconcile_dependencies`. That is the pinned ref, which is the first thing they asked for.

⭐ SO THE DEFECT IS NOT A MISSING NODE TYPE. It is that a first-time user, mid-build, could not find a tool that was already there — the same shape as the DesignRule report from the same document, where `find_tools` also came up empty. `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` names the mechanism: a typed tool with no instruction and no detector reaches nobody. This is the instruction leg missing on a tool that has the other two.

⚠️ AND THE SMALLER HALF IS GENUINELY UNHOUSED, so this must not be read as fully refuted. They also asked for 'a BRING-UP RECIPE, and a place to record FIXES PUSHED INTO IT'. `external_dependency` carries neither. They put the fixes in a Decision's prose — which is the workaround that this same day's other findings say goes stale unread. A dependency you SEND PATCHES TO is a different relationship from one you merely pin, and only the pin has a home.

COST, and it is the expensive kind: the workaround they chose attached test-bed configs to Verifications and fixes to Decision prose, so the design of a project whose ACCEPTANCE LAYER DEPENDS ON THREE EXTERNAL REPOSITORIES records those repositories nowhere a computation can read. Every seam, coverage and dependency answer for qs is silently scoped to what qs owns.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `external_dependency` would actually have satisfied them. It was never tried — by them or here — and its `graph_id` parameter suggests it is shaped for depending on ANOTHER REFLOW2 DESIGN, which a bluesky simulator is not. Reading the description is not running it.
properties.value: {"reported_by":"qs project, 2026-09-04, first use","claim":"the graph has no place for a repository we depend on but do not own","refuted_half":"external_dependency exists at built.rs:66 and records source, version, parts taken, forwarded switches","standing_half":"no bring-up recipe and nowhere to record fixes pushed upstream","real_defect":"instruction leg missing - no skill points at it, and find_tools did not surface it","untested":"whether it fits a non-reflow2 dependency; graph_id suggests it is shaped for reflow2 designs"}
